About this work

Veterum Sophorum Sigilla et Imagines Magicae — "The Seals and Magical Images of the Ancient Sages" — is a short astral-magical text: directions for cutting planetary seals and images into stones and gems, tied to the name Tetragrammaton and the planetary courses, "for the production of wonderful effects." It belongs to the later esoteric corpus attributed to Trithemius.

Attribution note. This text is not by Johannes Trithemius. It is a 17th-century astral-magic grimoire published under Trithemius's name in 1612 — a pseudo-Trithemian work of the Hermetic tradition, riding his posthumous occult reputation — and it should not be cited as Trithemius's own writing. It is retained here because it circulated under his name and forms part of the Trithemius legend.

This is the 1612 e-rara witness — the second of two printings of the text in the corpus, alongside the Marne / Aubry edition (prdl-70291). The Latin was re-OCR'd from the page scans and translated by GPT-5.5. No standard scholarly English translation is known; the text has circulated in the occult-manuscript tradition. A few passages are flagged where the source scan is weak; the translation otherwise sits in the top tier (S).

MAGICA. 7

TRACTATE II.

THE IMAGES, OR SEALS, OF CHAEL.

Chael, one of the sons of the sons of Israel, a very ancient teacher, when he was in the desert, observed and had many figures carved according to the course of the signs and planets, and recognized a very great effect in them. And so that these powers of the images might be known to posterity, he composed a book, from which the following have been excerpted. And blessed be God, who gave such powers to the earth for the salvation of the human race. (These words are found in the very book written by Chael, immediately at the beginning.)

The figure of a man sitting behind a plow, with a long beard, a long face, and curved eyebrows, on whose neck there are four men lying, and who holds a fox and a vulture in his hands: if such a stone, on which these things have been carved, is hung from the neck, it is effective for all planting and for finding treasures. For if, when going to bed, you place it beneath your neck, in sleep you will see treasures and the manner of extracting them. It also has another power, namely to help the illnesses of brute animals when they have drunk water in which this stone has been washed. It must be carved on the day and hour of Venus.

TRACTATE IV.

IMAGES, OR SEALS, of Thetel.

Thetel, a most ancient doctor, treating of carvings in stones, says that these carvings, when found in suitable stones, have very great power.

The image of a man carved in jasper, having a shield in his left hand and in his right an idol or something warlike, and in place of feet there are vipers, and in place of the man’s head there is the head of a cock or a lion, will give power against enemies and renders the wearer victorious. It is effective against poisons, and it also staunches blood from whatever part it flows.

The figure of a man having a little bundle of herb at his neck, when it has been carved in jasper, has the power of discerning or recognizing illnesses; it restrains blood from whatever place it flows. They say that Galen possessed this stone.

They say that a cross carved in green jasper

MAGICA. 21

has the power of freeing the wearer from drowning in water.

A woman holding a bird in one hand and a fish in the other, when she has been carved in chrysolite, is of great value for commerce.

The figure of a wolf carved in jasper is effective against cunning and prevents one from uttering insane words.

The figure of a stag carved in jasper has the power of healing and freeing lunatics and the frenzied.

The figure of an emperor carved in jasper with his head raised makes the wearer lovable to every creature, and he will obtain whatever he has asked for.

The figure of a virgin with a flowing garment, holding a laurel in her hand, when it has been carved in jasper, makes the wearer safe from drowning in water, nor will he be vexed by a demon; it makes him powerful and able to obtain all things.

The figure of a man having an inscribed palm branch in his hand, when it is found in jasper, makes the wearer powerful and pleasing to princes. Thus far Thetel.

SEALS

TRACTATE V.

IMAGES, OR SEALS, of Solomon.

A very ancient little book was found in the desert among the children of Israel, which, because many works of Solomon were found in it, was ascribed to Solomon. The title of the book was: On the Seals of Stones According to Your Name, O Lord, and According to the Course of the Stars.

The figure of a man sitting upon a plough, having a small neck and a long beard, and four men lying upon his neck, and holding a fox in one hand and a vulture in the other: you should know that this seal, hung from the neck, is effective for all plantings and for every discovery of treasures. You will establish the proof of it in this way: take pure black wool without dye, wrap the stone in it, place it among wheat chaff, and put it under your head; then in sleep you will see all the treasures of the region in which it is. At the same time it has the power of healing all the illnesses of beasts, if they drink the water in which it has been washed.

A horse bearing a crocodile on its back, carved in white jacinth, makes one lovable to men and beasts.

If the image of a man’s head with a long beard and a little blood about the neck is found carved in adamant, know that it confers victory and boldness, preserves the body from every injury, and is effective for obtaining favor from princes.

has very great power for taming any beast whatsoever; and it must be bound in a leaden ring.

When you find the figure of a turtle-dove carved in pangonius, the one who carries it in a leaden ring will never be wounded, nor will he receive harm, but he will be honored by everyone, especially by elders.

When you find carved in gold the figure of a bird holding a leaf in its mouth, and in its mouth and sight there is the head of a man or of a vulture, the one who carries it will gain profit from everything he is about to buy and sell, and he will be sought out by buyers.

When you find carved in crystal the figure of the face of a lion or dragon having two heads with a slender tail, or of a man in whose right hand there is a staff and who strikes the head of a lion, and you set it in orichalcum, with musk and amber beneath the stone, and carry it with you, all will obey you and you will increase your wealth. Wax sealed with it will have the same power.

When you find carved in some stone the figure of the winged horse called Pegasus, it is excellent for soldiers, and in field battle it gives boldness and eagerness.

The figure of a tree, or vine, or ear of grain carved on some stone makes the wearer abound in food and clothing, and renders princes favorable.

Mars armed, or a maiden in a stola with a flowing garment, holding laurel in her hand, if found on jasper, renders the wearer powerful in accomplishing deeds of arms, and frees him from violent death, from drowning in water, and from adverse misfortunes.

The figure of an armed man on a horse with a lance, carved on amethyst, makes the wearer victorious in war in the field.

The figure of Hercules, holding a club in his right hand and killing a lion or some other monster, if you find it carved on a stone, know that it grants victory in battle in the field.

The figure of Jupiter, which is in the form of a man with the head of a ram, makes the wearer lovable and quickly obtaining whatever he wishes.

A virgin or girl with a lamp, carved in crystal, has the power of preserving the light of the eyes.

The figure of the fiery triplicity, that is, of Aries, Leo, and Sagittarius, carved on a precious stone, is said to be effective for all cold illnesses

and to assist phlegmatic fevers; and, because of the dignity of the planets that hold dominion in those signs, to render the wearer pleasing to God and men, eloquent, endowed with talent, and able easily to obtain honors and dignities. It must be carved in such a way that, in the triangle, Leo holds the apex, Aries the right side of the base, and Sagittarius the left.

The image of the earthy triplicity, that is, of Taurus, Virgo, and Capricorn, engraved on a stone will provide help for all hot and moist illnesses, and will incline the wearer toward rural works, such as ploughing, planting, sowing, cultivating vineyards, and the like. Capricorn must be at the apex, Taurus on the right side of the base, and Virgo on the left.

The image of the airy triplicity, that is, of Gemini, Libra, and Aquarius, carved on a stone frees one from all cold and dry illnesses arising from melancholic humor, especially quartan fever. Libra will be at the point of the triangle, Aquarius on the right side of the base, and Gemini on the left.

The figure of the watery triplicity, that is, of Cancer, Scorpio, and Pisces, engraved on a stone frees one from hot and dry diseases, such as hectic fever, and from all diseases of choler; but it renders the wearer inconstant, unjust, and a hater of truth. Cancer must be at the crown of the triangle,

Pisces on the right side of the base, and Scorpio on the left.

The figure of Saturn engraved on stones is of this kind: an old man holding a sickle in his hand, having a beard that is not very hairy. This figure, carved on a stone of the nature of Saturn, renders the wearer powerful, with a continual increase of power.

The image of Jupiter is of a man sitting on a seat or on a four-footed chair, holding a rod in one hand and a ball in the other; or holding an image of Cancer or a fish, and having an eagle before his feet. But among the doctors of magic it is fashioned otherwise: for they carve the figure of a man with a ram’s head, wrinkled heels, and a slender chest. If this is engraved on a stone, especially krabatus, it renders the wearer fortunate, lovable, and pleasing to religious men, and raises him to honors and dignities.

The image of Mars is fashioned on stone in many ways: sometimes with a standard in his hand, sometimes with a lance or another instrument of war, yet always armed, and sometimes equestrian. The power of this stone, when carved in this way, renders the wearer victorious, bold, and warlike, especially if it is carved on a stone of similar virtue.

The figure of the Sun is found in different forms: sometimes in the likeness of the Sun, with rays all around,

sometimes in the likeness of a man sitting on a seat, with loose hair and flowing garment, and also in a chariot, as if he were being carried by four horses, so that the twelve signs of the zodiac are all around the chariot. The power of this figure carved on some stone renders the wearer commanding and pleasing to great men.

The images of Venus likewise are many; nevertheless the following is more frequently engraved on stones: a woman with a large garment and stola, holding laurel in her hand. Its power is to give agility in accomplishing tasks, to bring all things to the desired end, to remove fear of drowning in water, and to bring honors from women.

The figure of Mercury is a man with a slender chest, having a fine beard and winged sandals, holding the caduceus rod, with a rooster before his feet, or with a serpent under his feet. Its power is to assist in acquiring knowledge and oratory, and it also gives very great help in enriching merchants.

The images of the Moon are various. For sometimes she is fashioned in the proper figure of the Moon, with horns; sometimes in a chariot, as a girl with dogs and a quiver, with dogs following a stag. The power of this image is to provide success in legions, and from these good things, etc.

Seals

good things and honors, and in all matters being undertaken to provide speed and ease, and to bring everything to the desired end. But one must carefully observe, as was also warned above, that the planet whose image you wish to have carved in a suitable ring ought to be very well disposed, that is, not combust, retrograde, oppressed or touched by the rays of malefics, but in a good place of the heaven, at the Ascendant or Midheaven, with Jupiter or Venus, and in its essential dignities; otherwise the image will be empty and of no importance.

Moreover, the ancients formed the image of the Bear in this way.

They engrave two bears encircled by a serpent: the Greater Bear is contained at the head of the coil, the Lesser at the tail. This image, carved in some stone, makes the wearer learned, crafty, and powerful.

The image of the Crown has the likeness of a royal crown with many stars; sometimes it is figured in the likeness of a king with a crowned head. It is located in the northern part and in the sign of Sagittarius, and is of the nature of Venus and Mercury. When this image has been carved in stone, it gives honors and knowledge to those who wear it, and royal favor.

The image of Hercules Bent is also as follows:

Magic

A man fallen to his knees, holding a club in his hand and killing a lion; sometimes a man with a lion skin in his hand. Such figures, carved in a suitable stone, contribute to victory in war, especially if it is worn in agate.

The image of the Swan or Hen, with wings spread and neck bent, makes the wearer pleasing to the people, learned, and wealthy, and drives away gout, paralysis, and quartan fever.

The figure of Cepheus, having a sword girded on, with arms and hands spread out, carved in stone, makes one cautious and learned; and when it is placed beneath the pillow of a sleeper, it makes delightful things appear in sleep.

Cassiopeia is the image of a woman sitting in a chair, having her hands stretched out in the manner of a cross, sometimes with a triangle on her head. It is placed in the sign of Taurus and in the northern part. Its nature is of Saturn and Venus. When this has been carved in a suitable stone, its virtue will be to provide health to people, to restore weak and weary bodies, to give rest and tranquility to those who wear it after labor they have undertaken, and to provide pleasant and sweet sleep.

Seals

Andromeda is the image of a girl with disheveled hair and lowered hands. She is contained by Taurus in the north, and is of the nature of Venus. Its virtue, if it has been carved in stone, is to reconcile quarrels and disputes that have arisen between husband and wife, to strengthen stable love, and to guard against very many illnesses.

Perseus is an image holding a sword in the right hand and the head of the Gorgon in the left; it is located in Taurus and in the northern part. It has the force of Saturn and Venus. If it has been carved in stone, it turns misfortunes away from the wearer and preserves him from lightning and storm; not only the wearer, but also the places where it is kept. It also dissolves enchantments.

Serpentarius is the figure of a man holding a serpent, grasping its head in his right hand and its tail in his left. It is in the sign of Scorpio and in the north, and has the nature of Saturn and Mars. Its virtue, when carved in stone, is to be effective against poisons, to cure the bites of poisonous animals, and, if its washing is drunk, to make one vomit up poison without injury.

The Eagle, or Falling Vulture, is the image of an eagle flying with an arrow beneath its feet. It is located in Cancer and in the northern part, and is of the nature of Jupiter and Mars; but the arrow is of the nature of Mars and Venus. These constellations, when

Magic.

When these constellations have been engraved on a stone, they are said to preserve the bearer’s former ranks of honors, to acquire new ones, and to confer victory.

The Fish, or Dolphin, is the image of a humped fish. It is in the sign of Aquarius and in the north, having the nature of Saturn and Mars. When it has been engraved on a stone and bound to the limbs, it makes the bearer fortunate in fishing.

Pegasus, or the winged horse, according to some is half a horse with wings, according to others a whole horse with wings, and without a bridle. It is in the sign of Aries and in the northern part, having the nature of Mars and Jupiter. When it has been engraved on a stone, it gives the bearer victory in battle on open ground, and renders him swift, cautious, and bold. But when it is hung from a horse’s neck, or placed in the water where the horse drinks, it will free him from many illnesses.

Cetus is the figure of a great fish with a curved tail and a large mouth. It is contained by Taurus and in the southern part, and possesses the nature of Saturn. When this figure has been engraved on a stone, with a crested serpent above its back, it makes the bearer fortunate at sea, renders him prudent and lovable, and restores what has been taken away.

Seals.

The image of Orion is that of an armed man with a sword or sickle in his hand. It is placed in the sign of Gemini and in the southern part, and has the nature of Jupiter, Saturn, and Mars. This figure, engraved on a stone, renders the bearer victorious and makes him carry off victory over his enemies.

The image of the Ship has a curved prow and a raised sail, and sometimes is without oars and sometimes with them. It is contained by Leo and in the southern part, and is of the nature of Saturn and Mars. Engraved on a stone, it renders the bearer secure in affairs conducted on the sea and water, and does not permit him to receive harm from water.

The image of the Dog is the figure of a hunting dog with a curved tail. It is in the sign of Cancer and in the southern part, having the nature of Venus. If it is engraved on a stone, they say that it has the very power of completely freeing lunatics, maniacs, and those possessed by demons.

The image of the Hare is in the likeness of a hare, with ears and feet extended, as if it were running. It is placed in the sign of Gemini and in the southern part. Its nature is Saturnian and Mercurial. Its power is to cure the frenzied and to be effective against the wiles of demons; nor will the bearer be able to be harmed by a malignant spirit.

The Centaur is the figure of a bull as far as the neck, the rest being a man, holding in his left hand

Magic.

a spear resting above the left shoulder, with a hare hanging from it; and in his right hand a small beast lying on its back, with a kettle hanging. It is established in Libra and in the southern part, and is of the nature of Jupiter and Mars. The power of this engraving is to render the bearer constant and healthy with lasting health.

The image of a seated Dog in Cancer is of the nature of Venus. When it has been engraved on a stone and you have carried it with you, you will not fear dropsy, and you will be freed from plague and from a dog’s bite.

The figure of an altar or censer is of the nature of Venus and Mercury, with a kindled fire. When it has been engraved on a stone, it makes the bearer fit for summoning spirits, for being in converse with them, and renders them obedient. They also say that it renders the bearer adorned with perpetual virginity, since it induces chastity.

The image of Hydra, or the Serpent, is the figure of a serpent having above it an urn near the head, and a raven near the tail. It is of the nature of Saturn and Venus. Its power is to make the bearer very rich, astute, cautious, and free from harmful things, and it resists every harmful color.

The figure of the Southern Crown is made like an imperial crown. It is of the nature of Saturn and Mars, in

Its virtue lies in increasing wealth and in making a person cheerful and pleasant.

The image of the driver, or charioteer, is the figure of a man in a chariot, holding a goat on his left shoulder. It is placed in the sign of Gemini and in the north, having the nature of Mercury. This figure, carved in stone, makes the bearer a hunter and fortunate in catching animals.

The image of the banner is made in the likeness of a banner spread out at the end of a spear. This, carved in stone, makes the bearer fortunate in military service and victorious in battle fought in the field.

The image of the Lion, carved in gold when the Sun is in Leo and the Moon does not aspect Saturn, preserves one from stone and from hot diseases.

The image of the Scorpion, impressed or carved on a gold ring and bezoar stone when the Moon is in Scorpio, and Scorpio is thus in one of the angles of the world, is effective against the sting of a scorpion.

The image of Aquarius benefits those who have false imaginings, such as melancholics, those suffering quartan fevers, and maniacs. It must be made on the day of the Sun and in its hour, and Jupiter must not be combust, nor must the Sun be higher than Jupiter; nor must Saturn be in the Ascendant, nor in the 19th degree of Aries; the 3rd, 15th, or 27th of Taurus; the 11th of Gemini; the 3rd, 4th, or 12th 150

MAGIC. 41

15th, or 19th of Cancer; the 2nd, 5th, or 19th of Leo; the 3rd, 13th, or 30th of Virgo; the 3rd, 5th, or 21st of Libra; the 7th, 18th, 20th, or 21st of Scorpio; the 13th or 20th of Sagittarius; the 12th, 13th, or 24th of Capricorn; the 7th, 18th, or 20th of Aquarius; or the 13th or 29th of Pisces.

The image of Pisces, when the Sun is in Pisces in the twelfth house and the Moon is in the Ascendant, and when the lord of the Ascendant and the lord of the sixth house aspect one another by sextile or trine, or at least when the Moon aspects either one of them, is said by experience to free the bearer, under the soles of the feet, from gouty pains.

C S

42 SEALS

ON THE METHOD OF MAKING SEALS AND MAGICAL IMAGES.

TRACTATE VI.

Having set out the magical seals and images, and the method of making them, so far as it has indeed been handed down by the most ancient writers themselves, it remains that a more exact method of making them also be added here, and that the preceding matters be explained more precisely.

And indeed, before everything else, in their composition the time must be considered: the time of election, I mean, must be carefully observed in inscribing or carving figures on stones. For they receive a greater power from heaven if they are carved at fixed and suitable times, since in this way the stars exert their influence more strongly. Hence one who wishes to arouse love uses favorable aspects, but one who wishes to kindle hatred uses unfavorable ones. Therefore they wish the image of Saturn to be fashioned when he himself is in Capri-

MAGIC. 43

corn or Aquarius; that of Jupiter in Sagittarius and Pisces; that of Mars in Aries and Scorpio; that of the Sun in Leo; that of Venus in Taurus and Libra; that of Mercury in Gemini and Virgo; that of the Moon in Cancer. Thus the image of Leo or Cancer ought to be set into a ring or stone when the Sun is passing through Leo and the Moon through Cancer, yet in such a way that each is free from every impediment, and especially from the rays of Saturn or Mars.

It must also be held that any sign, so long as the Sun is in it, becomes living, rules the others, and has its effect felt before the others; and therefore the planet must always be directed to the place, that is, to the sign, face, and degree that the Sun illuminates.

Thus far concerning the magical images of the ancient sages. I have chosen to enumerate them here chiefly for this reason: so that it may be plain that they were constructed from the principles of magical philosophy, that is, of true and natural magic, not of Goetia and Necromancy; although it is certain that superstition has crept into many of them through abuse. Use has praise; abuse has blame. For if anyone should wish, with superstition, to direct them toward doing evil, he will be contrary to the divine order of the art itself and to the principles from which they flowed; and he should fear lest, ensnared by mad superstitions, he become wholly mad and superstitious.

Moreover

44 SEALS

Moreover, on almost the same foundations and for the same causes, gilded and silver plates, round, square, or triangular, have now also begun to be fashioned; on them certain signatures and characters of the planets are engraved according to certain positions and configurations of the heavens, or constellations, in order to obtain the favor and influence of each planet. For it is especially consonant with reason and experience that the influence of the planets is received and retained in figures and images of this kind, marked with a definite form and with images.

Meanwhile this must be observed with the greatest care: that the planet whose influence you seek be strong and fortunate, that is, in its own house, exaltation, or triplicity, in the eastern angle or midheaven, free from the harmful rays of Saturn or Mars, supported by the trine or sextile of Venus or Jupiter, or joined with them, direct, swift in motion, not combust, and ascending in the circle of its auge.

MAGIC. 45

THE ERECTION OF THE SIGNATURE of Mercury, for sharpening the memory.

Let Mercury serve as an example. If anyone wishes to obtain its influence for sharpening understanding, wit, and memory, he should observe at what time of the year Mercury is in Gemini or Virgo, the signs in which it has its own house, and is strong and fortunate in the east or in the midheaven. Once the hour and minute of the hour have been found, a careful and skillful engraving of the celestial figure, together with a delineation of the aspects, should be made in pure silver. This is afterward enclosed in white silk and kept; and, with a few grains of the best musk added, it is sewn into a cap at the part where it precisely touches the cerebellum. It has been observed to perform its operation chiefly at night, and more evidently at that hour and time at which the engraving was both begun and completed.

In this year 1608, Mercury was found strong and fortunate around 11 May, at the second hour of the morning. Again it will be strongest and most fortunate around the 14th and 15th day of the month of September, a little before and after the fifth hour of the morning, at which time it precedes the Sun in the eastern angle, in its own house, exaltation, and the favorable trine of Jupiter.

46 SEALS

And this is the method of sharpening the intellectual power and memory from the virtues of the heavens. From plants and animals too, I hope I shall gain no small favor among those whose memory is fragile and fluid, although they are quick in understanding, if I bring forth certain remedies for strengthening the memory. I know that very distinguished men have used them successfully; until now they have lain hidden among concealed secrets. I do not begrudge what can be of public use. You should know, however, that there are many things in them that adhere neither in temperament, nor in matter, nor in any manifest quality, but must be ascribed solely to some occult property.

Take seven hearts of swallows, still beating; two of turtledoves; dried mint, pennyroyal, vervain, eyebright, prepared coriander, galitrichum, each one ounce; flowers of rosemary, half an ounce; aromatic calamus and cinnamon, each two ounces; cloves, one and a half ounces; musk and musky Gallia, each six grains; anacardium honey and storax calamita, each half an ounce. Of these, let the ingredients that admit of grinding be reduced to a fine powder, and with fennel water let them be made into pastilles in the shape of a date-stone.

The person who will use this shall observe the following order. After the body has been purged, for fifty nights he shall eat nothing for supper except raisins with a few almonds and a little bread. His lunch

MAGIC. 47

will be either a roasted hen or a young chicken, a turtledove, a partridge, or something similar; his drink will be one-year-old wine, moderately diluted. Each night, near the hour of sleep, a pastille shall be inserted into the right nostril and stopped with cotton, and he shall keep it so no longer than it takes to recite twenty verses of Virgil. After several days have passed, put into the left nostril a pastille moistened with rosewater, and you will retain everything you are about to read, or will quickly grasp it with understanding.

But anyone who wishes in this way to preserve his memory completely must abstain from drunkenness, sex, and especially from an overloaded stomach, from all satiety, green fruits, vegetables, salted meats, and everything that generates wind. At the end of the meal, prepared coriander seed is to be used. Above all, it will also be harmless if it is carefully and properly prepared. It will also not be harmless to hold a pastille in the mouth from time to time and swallow it. It will also help to throw a pastille upon coals, so that the smoke may be properly received into the nostrils and, once received, retained, the nostrils being stopped with cotton so that it does not escape; or also to dissolve some pastilles in lavender water, rosewater, or anise water, and frequently, morning and evening, to moisten the forehead, temples, nostrils, and the back of the head around the capsule of memory, and to put clean soaked little linen cloths into the nostrils. And yet this remedy has been disclosed to few.

48 Seals

But to return to celestial matters: in precisely the same manner and form as with Mercury, the powers and influences of the remaining planets can be drawn down. Thus, for obtaining honors and dignities, and the favor and goodwill of princes and magnates, there is the image of the Sun when he is in Leo and in the tenth house, in trine with Jupiter or the Moon. Yet in this year 1608 the solar influence is impeded because of Mars opposite from Aquarius, as the remarkable and unusual changes of the very air clearly show. Hence, in forming these figures, this alone must be observed: that the planet whose virtue and influence one wishes to draw to oneself be as free as possible from every impediment.

Magic. 49

Demonstration of the Reasons Whence These Magical Images Have Such Great Force and Efficacy.

Treatise VII.

But why and whence rings, images, and figures engraved in a particular metal or stone possess the powers credited to them is not to be assigned to temperament, nor to manifest qualities, nor to the whole substance, but to a divine and magical cause, that is, to some higher and more sublime cause, which some have not inappropriately called a spiritual vehicle and bond. Through this mediation, body and soul, substances mutually distant, are joined together; by this the magnet draws iron, and chicory follows the motion of the Sun.

By this vehicle and bond intervening or coming between, Mercury is effective in quicksilver, in sharpening or weakening the memory and the cogitative faculty, in the alectorius stone, in a mixed color and flavor, and in Egypt, Greece, Flanders, and Silesia.

By this vehicle intervening, the Moon is effective in silver and glass, in the brain, in the left eye

50 Seals

of a man and the right eye of a woman, in the colors white, blue, and ash-gray, in a salty taste, in a moderate odor, in crystal, in the seventh climate, and in Flanders, Holland, Zeeland, and Denmark.

Saturn is effective in lead, the right ear, the spleen, bladder, and bones; in the colors black, livid, and leaden; in an astringent taste; in black and dark stones; in the first climate, the right side of the east, Saxony, Styria, etc.

Jupiter is effective in tin, the lung, ribs, pulse, seed, and left ear; in the colors dusky, purple, yellow, and green; in emerald, sapphire, and amethyst; in a sweet taste; in the second climate, the north, Babylonia, Persia, Hungary, and Spain.

The Sun is effective in laurel, the heart, arteries, the eye, and the right side; in the colors gold, saffron, and reddish-brown; in hyacinth; in a sharp and biting taste; in a good odor that is not excessive; in the fourth climate, and in the east.

Mars is effective in iron, the left ear, the gall, and kidneys; in jasper; in a bitter, bilious, and sharp taste; in the color red; in the third climate, the north, Sarmatia, Gaetulia, Lombardy, and Gothia.

Venus is effective in copper and mirrors of every kind; in the womb, kidneys, breasts, throat, genitals, and liver; in the color white; in a greasy, sweet, and fatty taste; in pearls, sapphire, and carbuncle; in the fifth climate, Austria, Arabia, Campania, Poland, and Switzerland.

Magic. 51

Therefore, to seek the principle of these hidden influences from those primary and manifest qualities, from temperament, or from the whole substance, is not so much absurd as ridiculous, since the actions of those from whom these virtues flow are not corporeal, and are poured in from heaven without a body. For this reason there is no need here for any measure taken from the senses, no ambitious battle of words, and no empty attempt at demonstrations. That the beginning of every philosophical demonstration cannot be sought from the senses and qualities, but must be sought elsewhere, is clear even from this common example: if someone asks about the color of the white rose, namely whence it derives its origin, and wishes to ascribe its cause to a colder temperament, what, I ask, will he say about the red rose? Will you say that species of endive pour out a milky juice because they are cold? Yet many very hot plants, such as the spurges, swell and drip with the same juice. And is aloe bitter for this reason, because it is hot? But in opium, which kills by its deadly coldness, there is a remarkable bitterness. And although it be granted that such things proceed from the property of the whole substance, nevertheless in our mystery a more sublime and more excellent craftsman, engraver, and fashioner must be placed and sought above that substance. Therefore the Alexandrians have tried in vain to refer everything to manifest qualities

52 SEALS

...are, which Scaliger, in Exercise 318, says is the height of impudence; and at least in the case of poisons it would have been proper for them to acquiesce. We see certain things spring forth from the lap and bosom of nature whose causes, although they are wholly inexplicable to us, nevertheless meanwhile it is pleasing and delightful to the lover of medicine, and to the diligent and keen investigator of natural things, to devise probable reasons for them. If he does not fully attain these reasons, still he does not take away trust from manifest facts, nor does he disparage the effects, but follows nature and its maker with admiration.

From this it is clear, and is elicited, that those things are not altogether vain which concern characteristic healing, which through engraved images hung from the neck accomplishes natural operations by the celestial properties of the stars, agreeing with our bodies by a wondrous influence. I say that those things are not plainly vain which the most ancient investigators of nature committed to letters and monuments concerning the written word, or characters and seals, fashioned at fixed times according to the power and influx of heaven, apart from every superstition, which ignorance alone of this mystery has invented, apart from profanation of the divine name and scandal, and apart from any violation of faith and religion. Although these things have hitherto, and especially in these last times, lain hidden, concealed and covered over among certain persons,

MAGIC.

who abused them rather than used them lawfully, since, having slipped into superstitions and not understanding the beginnings, they dared to attribute more to them than God, the creator of all things, granted and willed to be made manifest through them.

Yet I am so far from attributing any power in itself to these images, or affirming that a character or a named constellation has power by reason of its figure, since figure, number, magnitude, position, and the division of the continuous are the principles of no action, that I flatly deny that there is anything else acting and moving by whose power characters are effective. God heals human beings through the Prophets by the spoken word alone. For God is living; and the name of the living God is also living; and the letters of the living name are also living. God lives through himself; his name lives through him; and the letters live through the name. And just as God has life in himself, so also he gave to his name to have life in itself, and further gave the name to the letters.

Images or characters are therefore effective by reason of the power or office ordained by God or by nature for such a name or character. For there is no power either in heaven or on earth that does not descend from God. Thus medicines are visible bodies, words invisible bodies. Whether herb or word heals, God is in the cause, that is, the Spirit of God assisting nature

54 SEALS

through the word Fiat. Hence the herb itself is not medicine; rather, this medicine lies hidden invisibly in it, implanted there by God. Therefore things that are more remote from the senses and have hidden causes are not immediately to be condemned all the way to Orcus, nor mocked foolishly.

END.
